question: Which concurrency and batch setting improves task latency without failing correctness?
target_population: Fixture tasks; production transfer requires new representative tasks

factors.name: workers
factors.goal_contribution: More workers may reduce the time users wait for a completed task.
factors.potential_harm: Concurrent work may introduce races or lose task results.

factors.name: batch
factors.goal_contribution: Larger batches may reduce per-task overhead and shorten completion time.
factors.potential_harm: Batching may associate a result with the wrong task or omit a task.

objectives.name: latency_ms
objectives.measurement_method: Elapsed monotonic time after fixed warmup
objectives.validity_evidence: Synthetic fixture only; known output and timer sensitivity checks

objectives.name: correctness
objectives.measurement_method: Exact comparison of every task result with its known fixture answer
objectives.validity_evidence: Synthetic fixture only; a deliberately corrupted or missing task result fails the exact comparison

randomization: Randomize cells with recorded seed; pair arms on each task
blocking: Block by task; keep machine and provider version fixed
stopping_rule: Fixed budget; no repeated significance peeking
guard: All correctness checks pass; failed or absent guard blocks promotion

system_goal.purpose: Return correct task results promptly so users can complete their work.
system_goal.user: People using the task-processing application to complete a task.

success_criteria.description: Users receive a completed task result without unnecessary waiting.

protected_outcomes.description: Concurrency or batching must not change a correct result into an incorrect result.
